standard_prerequisites.name: Nonvanishing of a regular function over a component's generic point
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, the lemma that the local ring of a reduced ring at a minimal prime is a field, applied to the function corresponding to the section over an etale neighbourhood
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the conclusion that a nonzero section is nonzero at the generic point of each irreducible component of an affine etale neighbourhood.

core_obligations: Spread a nonzero section to the generic point (proof lines 2732-2740): for a nonzero section s and a point x in its support choose an affine etale neighbourhood on which the invertible module is trivial; the section corresponds to a nonzero regular function on the reduced scheme, hence is nonvanishing at the generic point of an irreducible component, so by the description of generic points of decent spaces the generic point of the space lies in the support of s.
Apply the same to the dual section (proof lines 2740-2744): the same argument shows that the generic point also lies in the support of a nonzero section t of the dual module.

Conclude (proof lines 2744-2748): the product st is a global function; it is nonzero because the local ring at the generic point is a field and both factors are nonzero there, and the ring of global functions is a field, so st is nowhere zero; hence the map given by multiplication by s is an isomorphism from the structure sheaf onto the invertible module.
proof_roadmap: Show that a nonzero section is nonzero at the generic point by trivializing on an affine etale neighbourhood.
Do the same for a section of the dual module.
Conclude that the product is a nonzero global function, hence everywhere invertible by the field property, and read off the triviality.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that an invertible module on a proper integral algebraic space over a field which has a nonzero section and whose dual has a nonzero section is trivial (statement lines 2724-2730). The proof (proof lines 2732-2749) shows that nonzero sections of the module and of its dual are nonzero at the generic point by trivializing on affine etale neighbourhoods, concludes that their product is a nonzero global function, and uses that the ring of global functions is a field to deduce that the product is nowhere zero and the module trivial. H2: a three-step argument with three inputs, written out in full.
